# The Linux Profiles this job proves against `ubuntu-24.04`. One name per line.
#
# A Profile leg only proves anything in a repository whose scale set actually
# serves that Profile. A scale set is registered on ONE repository or
# organization: a listener serving a Profile for another one cannot be assigned
# a job here, no matter how healthy it is. A job targeting a label nobody serves does not fail
# — it QUEUES, until the timeout kills it, and a timeout looks exactly like a
# runner that died. Listing a foreign Profile therefore manufactures a red run
# that says "the environment drifted" when the truth is "nobody serves this
# label here", which is the worst kind of false alarm: it is about the right
# subject and it is wrong.
#
# So this file names what serves THIS repository. Today that is
# `erainfra-canary-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404`, the scale set the daily smoke canary in
# .github/workflows/smoke.yml runs on and the only one registered here.
# `erainfra-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404` is deliberately absent: its scale set is
# registered on the bielcrystal-labs organization, so a leg for it would queue
# here forever. Add it the day a Worker serves it on this repository, and not
# before.
#
# The conformance job checks itself against this file rather than against the
# workflow's matrix, and refuses to report success unless every Profile named
# here produced a fingerprint in that run — so a leg dropped from the matrix,
# cancelled, or left queued fails the job instead of quietly reducing it to a
# comparison of `ubuntu-latest` against itself. Adding a name here without
# adding a matrix leg for it turns the job red, which is the intended order:
# declare what must be proven, then go and prove it.
erainfra-canary-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
